chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: How far she went in school and her extended family
summary: She went to the eleventh grade and finished high school; her mother and family helped with childcare.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. It's been almost two months since we've talked with you. A long time. Now the other thing that I wasn't clear about was whether you actually graduated from High School back in Homestead or whether you got your diplomma subsequently here in New York.
No, I went to the eleventh grade in Homestead High School and I got my diplomma after I came to New York.

Okay, I thought I wrote that someplace and I wasn't absolutely clear. Okay, I guess the final thing is the, whether you perceived any kind of conflicts from family, your son Orville was born back in Homestead, and did being a mother in any way limit your aspirations or affect your career in any way?

was quite small I was still near my mother and she helped me take care of him. When he was small I did little odd jobs around Homestead. I definitely didn't have any aspirations to make singing a career. I was singing for fun. And it wasn't until, say in later years, after my uncle Harry began taking me around with him that I became interested. And at that time my mother was still living and she took care of Orville.
And you had a wide extended family.
Okay, I think that just about does it with the Pittsburgh time. Unless there's anything you want to add.
No, that just about leads us up to when I left.
